scope.description: The generated test file plus one storage-level case over a single MemoryStorage instance in the same process; the case bypasses the protocol entirely and calls the storage trait's own append, trim, get_suffix and get_entries methods, reporting any panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot and is used as the storage's entry type, as in the rest of the harness.

Four entries are appended and two are trimmed, so a request below the trimmed index means an index of 0 or 1 while the trimmed index is 2; the case reads the storage's log length before and after the trim as the observable of the trim itself.
Panics are caught with catch_unwind around each storage call, so the build's overflow-check setting decides whether the unguarded subtraction panics and the run continues either way.
excluded: No cluster, no protocol messages and no snapshot path are exercised in the new case; it is a storage-level probe only.
Only the shipped in-memory storage is exercised; no other implementation of the Storage trait is available in this tree.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

basis.prefix: The new case starts from an empty MemoryStorage, appends four values, emits STORPROBE_BASE with the log length, trims two entries, then calls get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) each inside catch_unwind, calls get_suffix(2) at the trimmed index, and emits STORPROBE_RESULT with the log length, the two panic flags and the state and length of the read at the trimmed index. The lineage cases that share the execution are unchanged.

comparisons.description: A read below the trimmed index is reported or refused rather than aborting the caller, which is what the unguarded subtraction in the shipped in-memory storage would contradict.
The read at the trimmed index itself succeeds, so the probe distinguishes a below-trimmed request from an ordinary one.

before.description: Eight cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case drifts the recorded accepted indexes with three reconnection rounds, changes the leader so that the new leader's own recorded value is inflated too, and then calls the public trim(None) on that leader, wrapping the call so a panic is reported as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).

Three reconnection rounds of node 1 and node 2 are followed by node 2 taking the lead with try_become_leader(), which in this harness inflates the new leader's own recorded accepted index as witnessed by the staleleader stage.
trim is called with None, which the documentation describes as using the highest trimmable index; the call is wrapped in catch_unwind so a panic becomes a reported outcome.
excluded: Snapshots are not exercised; no entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in this case.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.
